name: Dukan diet

lead: The Dukan diet is a commercial high-protein, low-carbohydrate eating plan created by French physician Pierre Dukan. People follow it to lose weight quickly, and fat loss is the route to its looks payoff: a slimmer face, sharper jaw and cheek definition, and a leaner midsection.

The plan moves through four phases, starting with a protein-only stage and ending with a long-term maintenance stage. Published research on the plan itself is limited to reviews, surveys of what followers eat and case reports; no large controlled trial of the full programme is cited in the main reference sources.

paras: Followers work through the four named phases in order: Attack, Cruise, Consolidation and Stabilization. Early phases emphasise lean protein foods and restrict carbohydrates and fats; later phases reintroduce other foods in steps. Many followers pair it with walking or other activity and track weight on the scale.

Reviews note that high animal-protein intake can raise urinary calcium and lower citrate, which has been linked to higher kidney-stone risk. A case report described severe ketoacidosis within days of starting. A survey of Polish women on the plan found its food intake differed from standard recommendations. The British Dietetic Association has listed it among diets to avoid, and Pierre Dukan received a short ethics suspension in France in 2013.

chain: High-protein, low-carbohydrate eating with phased rules
angle.text: Followers use the plan to lose body fat on a structured schedule. As fat comes off, the face looks less full and the jaw, cheeks and midsection look more defined. The final phases are designed around keeping the lower weight.

lead: The Dukan diet is a high-protein, low-carbohydrate weight-loss programme devised by Pierre Dukan, a Paris general practitioner, and described in his 2000 book Je ne sais pas maigrir [1]. It is organised into four phases: Attack, Cruise, Consolidation and Stabilization [1].

People use it for appearance because losing body fat changes how the face and body read: reduced facial fullness, a more visible jaw and cheekbone structure, and a leaner waist. Followers describe the early protein-focused phase as producing quick scale results, which is a large part of its appeal.

Research on the Dukan plan specifically is limited. Narrative reviews discuss it alongside other popular diets [2][3], a Polish survey assessed what 51 women on the diet actually ate [4], and a case report and a kidney-stone review describe adverse events and risks [5][6]. Wikipedia notes that it is unclear whether the diet improves weight loss or glucose tolerance and cites no controlled trials [1].

paras: Pierre Dukan, a Paris general practitioner, says he began developing the approach in 1975 after treating a patient with obesity and looking for an alternative to the low-calorie, small-portion meals then standard [1]. He published it in 2000 in Je ne sais pas maigrir, which became a bestseller; the book appeared in the UK in 2010 and the US in 2011 [1].

The programme has four phases named Attack, Cruise, Consolidation and Stabilization, each with its own rules, and it presents itself as designed to prevent weight regain [1]. Reviews classify it with high-protein, low-carbohydrate diets such as the Atkins diet [2][3].

Dieters use it to reduce body fat so that facial and body contours show more clearly. Interest in the plan has been large enough to register in search data: an Italian analysis of internet searches found Dukan diet among the most searched diet terms before and during the COVID-19 pandemic [7].

No controlled trials of the full Dukan programme are cited in Wikipedia's summary of the diet [1]. Related published work includes a survey-based assessment of 51 Polish women following the diet, which analysed their intake of protein, fat, carbohydrate, vitamins and minerals from their reported menus [4]. A 2026 review compares the biochemical basis and metabolic consequences of the Dukan, ketogenic and low-glycemic-index diets [3], and a 2014 review discusses the Dukan diet alongside other popular approaches [6].

A review of fad diets and urinary stones says high-protein diets such as Dukan raise concern because animal protein can increase urinary calcium and decrease urinary citrate, giving a high overall lithogenic risk [2]. Wikipedia likewise notes kidney-stone concerns, particularly in people with a history of stones, along with some risk of chronic kidney disease and worsened cardiovascular health [1].
A 2014 case report described a 42-year-old woman who presented with intractable vomiting and severe ketoacidosis two days after starting the diet [5]. The authors described such events as rare.

The British Dietetic Association named the Dukan diet its number one diet to avoid [1]. In July 2011 a French court ruled against Dukan in a libel suit he brought against nutritionist Jean-Michel Cohen, who had criticised the diet in the press [1]. In 2013 Dukan was banned from practising as a GP in France for eight days for breaching medical ethics, related to a diet pill he had prescribed in the 1970s [1].
